blocks.goal: Extract the nested helper type definitions (TagName, AttributeKey, AttributeValue, Protocol, TypedValue) from Safelist into a new, dedicated production class to reduce the size and responsibility concentration of Safelist and to group related typed-value logic.

ops.details: Create a new production class org.jsoup.safety.SafelistTypes that contains the previously nested static classes: TypedValue (abstract) and its concrete typed subclasses TagName, AttributeKey, AttributeValue, Protocol. Move the full source of those nested classes from Safelist into SafelistTypes as static nested types (e.g., class SafelistTypes { static abstract class TypedValue { ... } static class TagName extends TypedValue { ... } ... }). Preserve the original constructors, methods (hashCode, equals, toString), and validation logic. Remove the moved nested classes from Safelist. Keep the new SafelistTypes class in the same package (org.jsoup.safety) and maintain the same package-private visibility for the nested types so Safelist can access them without changing package-level semantics.

Update all references in Safelist that previously referenced the nested types by simple name (TagName, AttributeKey, AttributeValue, Protocol, TypedValue) to qualify them via the new host type: SafelistTypes.TagName, SafelistTypes.AttributeKey, SafelistTypes.AttributeValue, SafelistTypes.Protocol, SafelistTypes.TypedValue. Update constructor calls, variable types, generics, and comparisons accordingly. For example, replace occurrences of 'TagName.valueOf(...)' with 'SafelistTypes.TagName.valueOf(...)' and type declarations 'TagName tag' with 'SafelistTypes.TagName tag'. No behavioral changes beyond type relocation. All updates are confined to Safelist.java so the block is self-contained.

Update related tests affected by this refactoring block so the configured build command passes. Adjust imports, package references, moved class references, constructors, and assertions only when required. Do not change production behavior through tests.
